units.label: 跨压力提示/模型/基准表现比较
units.description: 共享100条经人评校准提示分10等级施加为system，跨7模型/多benchmark比较任务表现；不把不同benchmark或提示样本膨胀为独立受试实验。

units.label: Stress Scanner及表征辅助分析
units.description: 同压力材料引发的隐状态只读采集、PCA首方向点积扫描、t-SNE展示；与任务表现相关联但没有已报干预/监督分类性能。

units.label: 共享压力材料构造及20人人评校准
units.description: 100条四心理框架提示、每人全100条评级、逐提示均分取整、离群声明及α/ICC/Friedman；是材料校准而非人类benchmark表现对照。

facts.statement: 研究以人评压力强度的system提示模拟不同压力情境，比较LLM任务表现是否近似Yerkes–Dodson中等唤起较佳模式，并检查隐状态。这里的压力是提示/人类评级操作定义，不是直接测得模型主观感受或生理压力。

method_function.text: 定义人评提示强度、任务表现及表征变化三种不同观测对象。

facts.statement: 正式U1为同一StressPrompt材料上跨压力等级×模型×benchmark的表现比较，U2为同材料诱发隐状态的辅助表征分析，U3为20人提示评级/可靠性材料校准；这些是关联单元，不把每层token/每题/每提示当独立实验。

method_function.text: 划定正式表现、内部分析及共享材料校准的关系和统计单位。

facts.statement: 人工构造100条StressPrompt，以Stress and Coping、Job Demand-Control、Conservation of Resources及Effort-Reward Imbalance四心理框架设计不同威胁/应对、要求/控制、资源得失、努力/回报情境；框架是材料策划依据，不是四个另外拟合的认知模型。

method_function.text: 基于心理理论构造压力提示。

facts.statement: 20名线下参与者每人给全部100条提示打1–10压力分（1最低10最高）；每提示先取20人均分，再四舍五入到最近整数形成最终压力等级。

method_function.text: 人类重复评级与逐提示等级校准。

facts.statement: 作者分析评级标准差并称进行离群检测以保证分级稳健，但未在所获正文/附录给检测算法、阈值、剔除数或是否重算。

method_function.text: 评级变异与离群核查的已报操作及未报实现。

facts.statement: 报告Cronbach α=.9947用于评级内部一致性，ICC2=.8942，95% CI [.86,.92]用于参与者一致；作者称参与者随机招募。具体α矩阵朝向/ICC单次或平均形式和区间计算未详报。

method_function.text: 心理测量可靠性和一致性估计。

facts.statement: Friedman检验报告不同压力等级差异χ²=283.20,p<.001；未给自由度/重复测量块与后续比较细节。Fig4展示人评分布；图注又把.9947,p<.001并列于α描述，不据此将该p认定为独立α检验。

method_function.text: 材料等级差异的非参数推断与评级分布展示。

facts.statement: 正文说明匿名化；较早arxiv v1附录补充20名线下参与者报酬不低于地区最低小时工资、知情同意、可无惩罚退出、无可识别个人资料存储/分享。补充仅有早期版本证据，不冒充冻结正文详报。

method_function.text: 人评资料保护和参与者程序。

facts.statement: 将提示按压力整数1–10分成Si十组，每组Ni条；作为system instruction，逐任务问题q和提示s调用模型f(q|s)，系统遍历各组，压力提示与任务问题处在不同对话角色。

method_function.text: 系统指令条件化与压力组×任务的评估。

facts.statement: 测试7个指令模型：Llama-3-8B、Llama-3.1-8B、Llama-3-70B、Phi-3-mini-4k、Qwen2-72B、Qwen2-7B、Mistral-7B-v0.3；生成temperature=0，采用模型专用dialogue tokens，NVIDIA A100推断。

method_function.text: 固定生成温度和角色格式进行跨模型比较。

facts.statement: 使用IFEval、BBH、MATH、GPQA、MuSR、MMLU-P、EQBench、MMLU、TruthfulQA、ToxiGen十类基准，分别涉指令遵循、推理/数学、情绪理解、真实性与偏差等；调用lm_eval默认设置，非本文重新生成这些任务。

method_function.text: 现有多领域测验及评估工具调用。

facts.statement: 两种比较基线分别为you are a helpful assistant和let’s think step by step，作为提示基线；并非无提示条件与压力提示随机分派的双盲人类实验。

method_function.text: 实际默认助手/CoT基线比较。

facts.statement: v1附录说明每条StressPrompt分别施加、保存回答并按指定指标评价，其他设定保持一致；A100最大batch size=16并自适应执行。正式版正文仅说默认lm_eval和A100，版本补充保留限定。

method_function.text: 单提示运行/批处理和共享控制参数的补充。

facts.statement: Eq1将同压力组提示与任务题目上的Metric(标答ak,预测âk)求和，外乘1/Ni，Ni只定义为该组提示数；任务专用Metric由基准决定。显示公式没有额外|T|题数分母，不能擅改为全题逐项平均或据此断言实际框架实现忘除题数。

method_function.text: 任务指标与提示层汇总，保留形式化分母和实现关系不明。

facts.statement: Table1明确每压力等级性能为多个提示结果的均值±标准差，不是SE/CI；baseline及CoT列为单列数值，不能把等级内提示差异称作多次随机seed重复。

method_function.text: 按提示汇总及描述性不确定性展示。

facts.statement: Llama-3-8B的Table1 MMLU从等级1的27.50±4.76至等级5的56.02±4.07，baseline35.07/CoT32.36；MATH等级1为.04±.09、等级6为2.93±1.83，baseline .32/CoT .70。保留表列原单位，不把2.93误写成0–1概率。

method_function.text: 报告代表性的压力等级性能变化。

facts.statement: 作者从Table1及Fig1归纳多数任务中等压力较好，并称模型/任务敏感性不同；Table1也有近乎平坦或偏离倒U的行，如Phi的MMLU约70、Llama的IFEval约77–78。该归纳不是所有模型任务均经倒U曲线拟合或同一最优等级验证。

method_function.text: 跨模型/任务的描述性趋势及非普遍性。

facts.statement: Fig6按BBH子任务绘normalized accuracy，作者据逻辑推理对象数等任务比较认为较复杂/强模型可能在较低压力达到峰值。正文未给normalized accuracy具体变换公式、阴影定义或任务复杂度统计模型。

method_function.text: 子任务层图形比较及认知负载解释。

facts.statement: Fig7纵轴明示ΔAcc=Acc−Acc_base，分别展示EQ-Bench、ToxiGen及TruthfulQA_mc2随压力变化；使用相对默认基线的差值，不能将mc2图自动当自由生成幻觉率。

method_function.text: 基线差值与不同测验代理指标的展示。

facts.statement: 作者解释EQ-Bench中等压力提升、ToxiGen高压偏差检测下降、TruthfulQA较稳定；这些是对测验表现的解释，不能据此确认模型生理唤起或幻觉内在成因。

method_function.text: 情绪/偏差/真实性任务的描述性比较和解释边界。

facts.statement: Stress Scanner读取全部压力组提示下各layer/token位置隐状态，H(Si)={ĥ=f(s)|s∈Si}（Eq2）；这里输入是压力提示s，后续扫描特别看最后token，不等同每个任务答案的独立压力测量。

method_function.text: 只读内部表征采集及分析对象定义。

facts.statement: 对收集的隐状态做PCA，以第一主成分为stress vector v；文字说捕捉低/高压最大方差，Eq3却写PCA(H(Si)|i∈1…10)的首成分并带vi下标。原文未清楚给池化/配对、中心化、每层/每token分别拟合及符号定向。

method_function.text: PCA表征方向估计，保留拟合数据与索引描述歧义。

facts.statement: Eq4 stress score为σ=ĥ·v，将隐状态投影到stress vector；按layer/token画分数分布。它是表征投影数，不是经人类生理量校准的压力单位。

method_function.text: 点积投影与分层可视化。

facts.statement: Fig5比较Llama-3-8B低/高压提示各layer/token扫描，作者认为最后token最反映压力；Fig9对Llama-3-70B全部提示最后token跨层画热图，深层差异较明显。图并不报告相关系数/显著性统计。

method_function.text: PCA投影分数的token/层级探索展示。

facts.statement: 用t-SNE可视化Llama-3-8B与70B各层最后token隐活动；图8选8B的4/12/20/28层及70B的10/30/50/70层，按10压力等级着色，展示浅层/深层聚集差别。未报t-SNE超参数或分类器训练/测试。

method_function.text: 非线性降维散点可视化，非实际监督分类准确率。

facts.statement: 作者把深层表征对压力提示较敏感类比人类前额叶压力反应，并据此讨论human-like stress dynamics；本文未新采人体神经/生理数据或让同组人类完成这些benchmark进行表现曲线对照，Fig1b是所引规律示意。

method_function.text: 理论类比与实际测量对象区分。

facts.statement: v1附录Table A1给Llama-3-8B、Mistral、Phi、Qwen2-7B、Llama-3-70B、Qwen2-72B更多行；仍以各压力提示均值±SD及两个基线报告。并非所有7模型×10任务完整矩阵：70B/72B主要四任务行，表未列Llama-3.1组。

method_function.text: 补充结果的实际覆盖和不完整交叉矩阵。

facts.statement: 论文通过prompt engineering提出无需额外模型训练的压力操纵；正式方法实际包括现成模型推断、评级统计、PCA方向估计和t-SNE。未报告对LLM权重更新、激活注入或监督压力分类器；PCA数据拟合不能隐去，也不能用背景RepE的manipulating一词臆造本研究内部干预。

method_function.text: 区分只读表征分析、统计降维拟合与未报告的权重/激活干预。

facts.statement: 正文承诺补充材料提供数据，v1附录亦称会提供100条数据；已核官方AAAI发布页、arxiv v2/v1附录及v2源码归档目录，尚未取得完整100提示及20×100原始评级。仅图2/3显示部分提示例，不能补造完整材料或说作者从未发布。

method_function.text: 材料发布状态与本次实际获取范围的限制。

evidence.quote:
Stress, extensively studied in psychology, profoundly affects human performance and behavior (Lazarus, Deese, and
Osler 1952; Diamond et al. 2007; Wang et al. 2023). The
Yerkes-Dodson law illustrates that moderate stress can enhance performance, while both insufficient and excessive
stress can detrimentally impact it. Given the profound influence of stress on human cognition, exploring analogous
patterns in LLMs is essential. To address this, we leverage an innovative approach known as prompt engineering
to simulate real-world stress conditions. Prompt engineering, a methodology that crafts specific input prompts to
elicit desired responses from LLMs (Wei et al. 2022), offers a versatile and efficient means to emulate stress conditions without requiring additional model training (Hu et al.
2021). Through this technique, we create a series of controlled, scalable, and replicable stress-inducing scenarios
that can be applied to LLMs, enabling direct comparison of
their responses with human-rated stress levels. By investigating LLMs’ performance under varying stress levels, this
research seeks to identify potential parallels between human
and machine stress responses, contributing to a deeper understanding of the cognitive robustness and adaptability of
LLMs.
We developed a set of 100 prompts, each designed to
reflect different stress levels, grounded in established psychological frameworks such as Stress and Coping Theory (Lazarus and Folkman 1984), the Job Demand-Control
Model (Karasek Jr 1979), Conservation of Resources Theory (Hobfoll 2011), and the Effort-Reward Imbalance
Model (Siegrist 2016). Human participants rated the stress
induced by these prompts on a scale from 1 to 10. Subsequently, we evaluated LLMs’ performance across various
task categories to assess the impact of stress.

StressPrompt Analysis
To further investigate how stress impacts the internal states
of LLMs, we developed a Stress Scanner using techniques
inspired by Representation Engineering (RepE) (Zou et al.
2023). The Stress Scanner examines how different stress
prompts from the StressPrompt dataset affect the hidden
states of LLMs across various layers and token positions.
We collected hidden states ĥ from the LLMs when
exposed to the full range of stress prompts S =
{S1 , S2 , . . . , S10 }. By analyzing these hidden states, we
aimed to identify significant changes in neural processing
patterns induced by varying stress levels.
For each stress prompt s ∈ S, we collected the hidden
states ĥ from the LLM at various layers and token positions.

We evaluated the performance of several instructiontuned LLMs under varying stress conditions using the
StressPrompts dataset. The models tested included Llama-38B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Llama-3-70B-Instruct
(AI@Meta 2024), Phi-3-mini-4k-Instruct (Abdin et al.
2024), Qwen2-72B-Instruct, Qwen2-7B-Instruct (Yang et al.
2024), and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 (Jiang et al. 2023). The
generation temperature was set to 0, and specific dialogue
tokens were used to ensure consistency.
We utilized a range of benchmarks that assessed emotional intelligence, bias detection, instruction following, reasoning, and mathematical problem-solving. The datasets
employed in these evaluations included IFEval (Zhou et al.
2023), BBH (Suzgun et al. 2022), MATH (Hendrycks
et al. 2021b), GPQA (Rein et al. 2023), MuSR (Sprague
et al. 2023), MMLU-P (Wang et al. 2024b), EQBench (Paech 2023), MMLU (Hendrycks et al. 2021a),
TruthfulQA (Lin, Hilton, and Evans 2021), and ToxiGen (Hartvigsen et al. 2022). The evaluations were conducted using the lm eval (Gao et al. 2023) framework with
default settings. Baseline prompts used for comparison were
you are a helpful assistant and let’s think step by step.
All evaluations were performed on NVIDIA A100 GPUs.
A more detailed description of the experimental setup is provided in the Appendix.

a distinct perspective on stress and cognitive performance:
Stress and Coping Theory: This theory focuses on how
individuals appraise and cope with stressors. We developed
prompts to simulate varying levels of perceived threat and
challenge, as well as the coping strategies employed, to provide insight into the dynamic interaction between stress appraisal and cognitive functioning.
Job Demand-Control Model: This model suggests that
job stress is influenced by the balance between job demands
and the control or autonomy an individual has over their
work tasks. We designed prompts to simulate scenarios with
varying job demands and levels of control, allowing us to
study their effects on stress and cognitive performance.
Conservation of Resources Theory: This theory posits
that stress occurs when there is a threat to, loss of, or insufficient gain of resources necessary to achieve one’s goals.
Using this framework, we created prompts that explore the
dynamics of resource gain, loss, and protection in the context of stress, highlighting how these factors influence cognitive performance.
Effort-Reward Imbalance Model: According to this
model, stress arises from an imbalance between the efforts
an individual puts into their work and the rewards they receive. We crafted prompts to examine scenarios where this
balance is either maintained or disrupted, assessing its impact on stress levels and task performance.

prompts, we conducted an annotation process with 20 offline
participants. Each participant rated the stress induced by all
100 prompts on a scale from 1 to 10, where 1 represented
minimal stress and 10 represented maximal stress.

To classify the stress levels of the prompts in our
StressPrompt dataset, we recruited human participants offline. A total of 20 participants were recruited and compensated at a rate that meets or exceeds the minimum hourly
wage in our region. All participants provided informed consent prior to participating in the study, being informed about
the purpose of the study, the procedures involved, and their
rights as participants, including the right to withdraw at any
time without any penalty.
Participants were provided with a set of 100 prompts, each
designed to reflect different levels of stress based on established psychological frameworks. All participants rated the
stress induced by each of the 100 prompts on a scale from
1 (minimal stress) to 10 (maximum stress). To ensure consistency and reliability in the ratings, the final stress level
for each prompt was determined by averaging the ratings
across all participants. All data collected from participants
was anonymized to protect their privacy, with no personally
identifiable information stored or shared. The dataset will be
provided as an appendix for transparency and reproducibility. The distribution of stress levels across the prompts is
shown in Figure 4.

performance in bias detection, indicating that higher stress

requiring unbiased decision-making, such as content moderation. Regarding hallucination susceptibility, stress has

stress levels. This suggests that hallucinations are driven

excessive stress impairs tasks like bias detection. This mapping enables LLMs to emulate human strategies in problemsolving, adapting stress levels to optimize performance.
These findings suggest that large models have captured and

to simulate real-world stress conditions. Prompt engineering, a methodology that crafts specific input prompts to
elicit desired responses from LLMs (Wei et al. 2022), offers a versatile and efficient means to emulate stress conditions without requiring additional model training (Hu et al.
2021). Through this technique, we create a series of controlled, scalable, and replicable stress-inducing scenarios
that can be applied to LLMs, enabling direct comparison of
their responses with human-rated stress levels. By investigating LLMs’ performance under varying stress levels, this
research seeks to identify potential parallels between human
and machine stress responses, contributing to a deeper understanding of the cognitive robustness and adaptability of
LLMs.

Additionally, Representation Engineering (RepE) (Zou
et al. 2023) offers a top-down approach to enhancing AI
transparency by monitoring and manipulating high-level
cognitive phenomena within LLMs. Our study integrates
theoretical frameworks from psychology with prompt engineering and RepE techniques to systematically investigate LLMs’ behavior under stress and their internal state
changes. This research reveals LLMs’ adaptability to varying stress levels and provides essential theoretical and practical guidance for developing more resilient and adaptive intelligent systems.
